questions.q:
Assertion (A) $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Cd}^{2+}$ are separated by first adding $\mathrm{KCN}$ solution and then passing $\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{~S}$ gas.
Reason (R) $\mathrm{KCN}$ reduces $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}$ to $\mathrm{Cu}^{+}$and forms a complex with it.
The correct answer is
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is true but (R) is not true
(A) is not true but (R) is true
questions.solution: $\mathrm{KCN}$ forms complex with $\mathrm{Cu}^{+}$and $\mathrm{Cd}^{2+}$ as $\mathrm{K}_{3}\left[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}\right]$ and $\mathrm{K}_{2}\left[\mathrm{Cd}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}\right]$ respectively. On passing $\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{~S}$, only $\mathrm{Cd}^{2+}$ complex gets decomposed to yellow CDS.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Upon heating a borax bead dipped in cupric sulphate in a luminous flame, the colour of the bead becomes green.
Statement II : The green colour observed is due to the formation of copper(I) metaborate In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
questions.solution: Upon heating a borax bead dipped in cupric sulphate in a luminous flame, the colour of the bead becomes blue. Blue colour is observed due to copper (II) metaborate while copper (I) is colourless,

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Colourless cupric metaborate is reduced to cuprous metaborate in a luminous flame.

Statement II: Cuprous metaborate is obtained by heating boric anhydride and copper sulphate in a non-luminous flame.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> is false but Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> is true
Both Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> and Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> are false
Both Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> and Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> are true
Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> is true but Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> is false
questions.solution:
(i) Blue cupric metaborate is reduced to colourless cuprous metaborate in a luminous flame

(ii) Cupric metaborate is obtained by heating boric anhydride and copper sulphate in a non-luminous flame.

questions.q:
The correct match between item 'I' and item 'II' is
Item I (Compound) Item II (Reagent)
(1) Lysine (P) 1-naphthol
(2) Furfural (Q) ninhydrin
(3) Isopropyl alcohol (R) KMnO4
(4) Vinyl benzene (Styrene) (S) Ceric ammonium Nitrate
questions.solution:
Lysine (amino acid) can be tested by ninhydrin as ninhydrin test is used for testing amino acids.
Furfural can be tested by 1-naphthol.
Isopropyl alcohol can be tested by Ceric ammonium nitrate which is a yellow reagent and on reaction with alcohol changes to red.
Vinyl benzene (Styrene) can be tested by KMnO4 as styrene decolourises alk. KMnO4 due to presence of unsaturation (double bond).

questions.q:
Match the flame colours of the alkaline earth metal salts in the Bunsen burner
$\begin{array}{l|l}
\hline \text{A. Caicium} & \text{p. Brick red} \\
\hline \text{B. Strontium} & \text{q. Apple green} \\
\hline \text{C. Barium} & \text{r. Crimson} \\
\hline
\end{array}
questions.solution:
Flame colours are produced from the movement of the electrons in the metal ions present in the compounds.
Calcium gives brick red colour. Strontium gives crimson colour. Barium gives apple green colour.
